question: does shrinkage whitening repair the key collapse while keeping the carrier that lets a synonym wording reach its own written key?

criteria.C1_control_identity: with the raw transform the runner's own read reproduces the real addressed_read on all 154 queries: identical fast sha, top slot and max|delta| = 0
criteria.C2_store_immutable: whitening is read-time only: store_keys/store_values/store_age hashes are identical before and after every whitening pass
criteria.C3_transform_scope: the same W is applied to the occupied stored keys and to the query key; the store keeps the raw keys and the encoder is untouched
criteria.C4_shrinkage_rule: the ridge is lambda = trace(Sigma)/d with Sigma the covariance of the occupied store keys about their mean; the value is fixed by this rule before any reading and is not searched
criteria.C5_threshold_source: the gate threshold is the minimum top cosine of the written group in that same arm; no negative label enters the value
criteria.C6_collapse_fixed: collapse_fixed = whitened effective rank >= 2x the raw effective rank, or whitened top_share <= 0.75 (thresholds fixed before the reading)
criteria.V1_written_bytes: if whitening changes the returned fast sha of any of the 22 written faces against arm A, the verdict is whitening_changes_written_bytes (hard failure, dominant rule)
criteria.V2_enables: otherwise, if at least two gaps are > 0 and the unwritten correct count does not drop, the verdict is whitening_enables_gate with the threshold interval (lower, upper]
criteria.V3_ceiling: otherwise, if whitening either fixes the collapse or keeps the carrier but not both, the verdict is encoding_is_the_ceiling: the averaged-pooling byte encoding ties the two together, so neither the gate nor the offset nor another linear form can separate them
criteria.unchanged: no fixture, face, position, class, ridge or anchor is retuned after first reading

transform.applied_to: occupied stored keys and query key, at read time
